# Independently verified triples

Canonical table: `data/triples.csv`. Every row was checked in this repo
with `fractions.Fraction` and the integer residual

```
4*x*y*z - n*(x*y + x*z + y*z) == 0
```

All 77 rows are Mordell-hard (`n ≡ 1, 121, 169, 289, 361, or 529
(mod 840)`). Multiple triples for the same `n` are kept; they are
different constructions, not duplicates.

Hard first-`R` (search depth of the first remaining denominator), from
the Heavy / Opus chats:

| n | first-R | n mod 840 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8803369 | 107 | 169 |
| 287567281 | 83 | 1 |
| 794037841 | 63 | 121 |
| 496609 | 51 | 169 |
| 586775809 | 63 | 529 |
| 3434195209 | 83 | 529 |

`make check` / `erdos-straus check-csv` must stay green if you add a
row.

Opus turn 8 (Type I harvest at \(N = 10^7\)) produced **no new
triples**.

Efficiency-test wave 1 (2026-09-06) added six Type I triples: the
first Mordell prime \(> 10^7\) in each leftover class. Wave 2 added
the first leftover prime \(> 2\times 10^7\) and then \(> 5\times 10^7\)
in each class. Wave 3 added the first leftover prime \(> 10^8\) in
each class. Wave 4 added the first leftover prime \(> 2\times 10^8\)
in each class and the deepest \(n\equiv 529\) first-R in
\([5.70\times 10^8, 8.00\times 10^8)\). Each row has residual \(0\).
They are constructions, not a cover.
